definition: A good wind farm site needs consistent wind, sufficiently high wind speeds, and enough available land for the installation.
core_idea: Coastlines and flat plains are generally the most attractive wind farm locations, while mountainous or uneven terrain is less attractive due to limited space and unpredictable wind behavior.
key_points: Three siting criteria: consistency of wind, sufficient wind speed, and adequate land availability.
Coastlines and flat plains are typically the easiest locations to develop.
Mountains/uneven terrain are less attractive because of space constraints and unpredictable wind.
The U.S. National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) is the primary source of U.S. wind resource data, building on long-standing government wind research originally done for aviation purposes.
relationships: Related to turbine spacing/wake effects, which further constrains site layout
